title: Public Interest Media Advocate Bill 2013
portfolio: Broadband, Communications and the Digital Economy

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create an independent Public Interest Media Advocate to carry out functions under companion proposals covering news media self-regulation and changes in media control.
The minister would appoint a qualified person part time for up to five years, with the office protected from directions by ministers or government.
Its principal regulatory functions would come from the accompanying self-regulation and news media diversity bills, while this bill would provide appointment and operational arrangements.
changes: The office holder would have to disclose interests that conflict, or could conflict, with the role.
The Advocate would be able to hold hearings when carrying out its functions.
Information sharing would be permitted where it assists another authority’s functions, with conditions available on disclosure.
An annual report would have to be provided to the minister for presentation to Parliament.
summary.affected: The Public Interest Media Advocate is affected.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Moved the Public Interest Media Advocate Bill 2013, proposing an independent statutory office to decide news media diversity transactions, assess self-regulatory schemes and complaints processes, and operate without ministerial or government direction.

speeches.speaker: Simon Birmingham
speeches.brief: Minister Conroy confirmed no one has been approached for the Public Interest Media Advocate role and that the government will follow Nolan principles and consult on appointments, defending the legislative process by citing two inquiries and extensive public debate.
